To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the charm quark transport coefficient in the QGP is large and its contribution to the di-electrons in the mass range 0.3-1.5 GeV is significant.
the charm quarks in medium are not so different from the ones in vacuum.
The charm quarks are produced by initial hard collisions and traverse a hot and dense fireball.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of charm and light quarks in the hot and dense medium and its implication on the di-electron invariant-mass spectra.
the dynamics of charm and light quarks in the thermalized medium and its implication on the di-electron production in heavy ion collisions.
the study of charm quark dynamics in the partonic matter and its implication to experimental observables in heavy ion collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
charm quarks in a medium are not a good candidate for a thermalization mechanism of the medium.
the charm quark dynamics in the thermal medium and the subsequent di-electron spectra are well understood by the present approach, and the charm quark contribution in the thermal medium is not large.
the di-electron invariant spectra in the low mass region $1.1\leq M\leq 2.5~ \mathrm{GeV/c^{2}}$ are dominated by semi-leptonic decays of charm quarks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the charm quark dynamics in medium is important and it can be studied in di-electron spectra.
charm quark dynamics is well understood by the Langevin equation with the transport coefficients calculated in the T-matrix method.
the charm quark transport is essential to the interpretation of di-electron data in relativistic heavy-ion collisions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
charm quark interactions with the medium can be important in the di-electron production in heavy ion collisions.
the medium effect on the charm quark dynamics can be tested in di-electron spectra and angular correlations at the RHIC.

the medium modification of the charm quark is not large at the RHIC and the di-electron spectrum in Au+Au collisions is mainly dominated by semi-leptonic decays of charmed hadrons, which are not affected by the medium.
